# Session Windows — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Session Windows. Run status: COMPLETED.

## How it works

- [statement] In Atlas, $sessionWindow runs a nested aggregation pipeline over each session and releases its results to the next stage when that window closes. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md · keywords: Session Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/windows.md
- [statement] Atlas event-time sessions close when the watermark advances beyond the session’s maximum event timestamp plus gap and allowedLateness. Their start is the earliest event timestamp; their end is the latest event timestamp plus gap. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md
- [statement] Atlas sends documents to the DLQ when partitionBy evaluation fails, or when an event is older than the latest source watermark and has no open session. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md
- [statement] A practical Atlas pattern groups shopping activity by user, aggregates each session, and triggers downstream abandoned-cart actions after inactivity. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/product-release-announcements/mongodb-atlas-stream-processing-now-supports-session-windows · keywords: Session Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Session windows group activity into variable-length sessions separated by an inactivity gap; partitioning by user or device keeps each entity’s sessions independent. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md · keywords: Session Windows · also: https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/streaming/apis-on-dataframes-and-datasets.html, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/stream-analytics-query/session-window-azure-stream-analytics
- [statement] An out-of-order Atlas event can bridge and merge two open sessions belonging to the same partition. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md
- [statement] Atlas requires gap and pipeline. partitionBy is optional: omission puts every document into one null partition. Only a single field or simple expression is supported, not multi-key embedded documents. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md
- [statement] Atlas defaults boundary to eventTime and allowedLateness to three seconds; specifying allowedLateness with boundary: processingTime is prohibited. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md
- [statement] Do not assume session APIs are interchangeable: Azure exposes timeout and maximum duration, while Atlas’s documented $sessionWindow parameters expose gap and allowedLateness without a maximum-duration parameter. (medium confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/stream-analytics-query/session-window-azure-stream-analytics · keywords: Session Windows · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md
- [statement] Implementation semantics differ: Azure documents a maximum-duration parameter, while Spark accepts dynamic per-row gaps. Neither option appears in the cited Atlas session-stage syntax. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/stream-analytics-query/session-window-azure-stream-analytics · keywords: Session Windows · also: https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/streaming/apis-on-dataframes-and-datasets.html, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-stream-processing/sp-agg-session.md
